lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Themes: the Display menu switches between the project, user, and default colours
lines.text: The theme is one file, `.comprehende/theme.json`. The CLI reads it at the root of the repository under review and in the home folder (`~/.comprehende/theme.json`). `serve` and `export` apply the repository file when there is one, else the home file, and an export carries both to the hosted page; the user switches between them in the UI. The two never merge. Write the repository file unless the user asks for a theme for every repository.

lines.text: Every key is optional. A token the file leaves out keeps the default colour. Each value is a literal colour: hex, or a colour function such as `rgb()`, `hsl()`, or `oklch()`. `radius` is a length in `rem` or `px`.

lines.text: - **Surfaces:** `background` (the page), `card` (panels and the diff frame), `popover` (menus), `secondary`, `muted`, `accent` (quiet fills: chips, hover, the selected row), `border`, `input`.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Themes: a .comprehende/theme.json sets the UI colours
lines.text: - **Text:** `foreground`, `card-foreground`, `popover-foreground`, `secondary-foreground`, `accent-foreground`, and `muted-foreground` (secondary text).

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Themes: a .comprehende/theme.json sets the UI colours
lines.text: - **Brand:** `primary` (links, the active item, buttons), `primary-foreground` (text on `primary`), `ring` (focus outline).

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Themes: a .comprehende/theme.json sets the UI colours
lines.text: - **Meaning:** `add` and `del` (added and deleted lines and counts), `warn` (attention), `destructive` (errors), `moved` (moved lines).

lines.author: Máté Molnár

lines.text: - **Stories:** `strand-0` to `strand-5`, one colour per story in the overview.

lines.text: ## Steps

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Themes: a .comprehende/theme.json sets the UI colours

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: theme steps from two simulated cigster runs
lines.text: 1. **Read the design language.** Find where the project defines its colours: CSS variables in a global stylesheet, a Tailwind `@theme` or config, a design-token file, or a component library theme. One `git grep` batch for definitions (`--background:`, `--primary:`, `@theme`, `colors:`), with vendored folders and lockfiles left out, finds them; a file that only reads `var(--primary)` is not a source. Read each defining file whole. When a value names a palette step from a package (`var(--color-slate-900)`, `amber-400`), read the colour from that package's source at the version the lockfile pins, such as its theme file in `node_modules`, or from its docs. Done when you can name the project's page, surface, text, border, and brand colours as literal values, and each mode it supports.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Themes: a .comprehende/theme.json sets the UI colours

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Skill: theme steps from two simulated cigster runs
lines.text: 2. **Map the colours.** Give each surface, text, and brand token the project colour with the same role, and set `radius` to the project's radius. A token with no project colour takes the colour of the nearest role: `popover` from `card`. Write both `light` and `dark`. When the project has one mode, make the other from the same palette: mirror the palette's lightness scale (the darkest surface becomes the lightest, and text goes the other way), and keep the brand colour family, darker or lighter until it reads on the new page; `primary-foreground` flips with it. Keep `add` green and `del` red, because the reader takes them as added and deleted lines; set them, `strand-*`, and the `diff-*` tokens only when the project defines its own colours for those roles. `warn` marks attention and is amber by default; when `primary` is near amber, set `warn` to a hue apart from `primary`, `add`, `del`, and `destructive` in both modes, such as violet. Check contrast as WCAG ratios: 4.5:1 or more for each `*-foreground` on its surface, `muted-foreground`, `primary`, and `destructive` on `background`. Done when every value is a literal colour, each mode has its surface, text, and brand tokens, and each pair passes.
